## Ruling 1 · ⚠️ The defect is bigger than "the census is three, not four" — I measured a second site the card does not name

`git grep` on `origin/main` @ `aa5994e17` puts *"four seams"* / *"all four seams"* in **at least six** places in this one file — `:55`, `:61`, `:91-92`, `:197-198`, `:481`, `:505`. ⛔ Re-derive that count yourself and reverse-check every hit; mine is a sample of a population I did not exhaustively sweep, and #12579 was short by one for exactly that reason.

⭐ **And `:505-511` is the sharp one.** The file states a falsifier so *"the next reader inherits a measurement instead of an argument"*, and lists three ways to reach it. The third is:

> *"… or a `resolveExecutionContext` that throws one synchronously. On that day the disclosure becomes live, this block's premise is false, and the fork has to be RE-OPENED."*

Under this card's measurement — `private async resolveExecCtx` at `:1453`, called as `.catch(() => undefined)` at `:1483` — that limb is **unreachable by construction**, not merely unobserved. ⇒ a falsifier that cannot be reached is not a falsifier, and a reader inheriting it believes this block is more testable than it is. That is worse than the miscount, and it is the same failure class: a true statement (the block's premise holds) carrying a false account of *why*.

## Ruling 2 · ⛔ Do NOT delete the `resolveExecutionContext` case

`:224`'s `vi.fn(() => { throw error; })` still pins something real — how the door behaves when an injected resolver throws — and `reached()` keeps it from going vacuous. It simply is not **evidence about a production path**. ⇒ **relabel it accurately; do not remove it.** Deleting a test to make a census true is the census lying in the other direction.

⭐ The honest shape is three production seams **plus** one declared test-only injection point, with the reason stated once and cited from the other sites rather than restated at each — this lane spent a whole card (#12579) on what happens when one explanation gets four copies.

## Ruling 3 · Measure the seam, do not infer it

⛔ Do not take `private async` + `.catch()` from this card. Read `packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts` yourself (**reading is not editing** — the fence bars writes) and state, with line anchors on the ref you measured:

- what `resolveExecCtx`'s declaration is,

⚠️ Then reverse-check the other three seams are genuinely production-reachable before you call the census three. ⛔ A census that corrects one number by assuming three others is not a measurement.

## Ruling 4 · `Part of #12537`, not a closing keyword

Fork (b) is real and unanswerable here. ⇒ ship `Part of #12537` so the card survives to carry it, and make every note you write point at #12537 as where that half is open.

⚠️ **If your measurement says otherwise, say so.** If you find the swallow at `:1483` is deliberate and already documented — so that nothing in `rest-server.ts` needs to change for the record to be honest — then this diff discharges the card and `Fixes` is right. ⭐ Flag the conflict; ⛔ do not silently pick either side.

- Run the suite. `package-door-declared-code.test.ts` is 155 cases across 4 sections; state files/tests passed. ⛔ Declare any narrowing rather than implying a full run.

- ⛔ **Do not edit** `packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts`, `packages/rest/src/rest.test.ts`, or anything under `packages/client/src/` — all held by PR #12421. ⛔ `packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts` is held by PR #12636; `packages/cli/test/helpers/serve-process.ts` and `packages/cli/test/serve-built-cli-prerequisite.test.ts` by #12618, dispatched in parallel.
- ⭐ **Report what you measure; ⛔ do not reconcile.** Distrust every number above, mine included.
- ⚠️ **GitHub writes go through the MCP GitHub tools.** Raw REST with `$GITHUB_TOKEN` is 403 for reads *and* writes. ⚠️ The **additive** label endpoint is also 403 — read, union, whole-set write, then read back. File out-of-scope findings yourself, **unlabelled**.

## ✅ ACCEPT — [PR #12646](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pull/12646), fork (a). ⭐ Three of my numbers were wrong and the dev caught all three

Verified against `origin/main`, not the report: one file, `+91/−14`, every hunk inside a docblock or a `//` comment.

### ⚠️ My census was wrong in BOTH directions, and the mechanism is worth more than the correction

I gave six sites. The dev gave six. **They are not the same six.**

**Short by `:262`** — `// 1. The demote reaches the wire, at every seam this door has`. A census claim spelled **without the word "four"**, so no grep for `four` can reach it. ⛔ And it was in my own first grep output; I read past it because I was matching on the token, not on the claim.

**Long by `:91-92`** — and the reason I had it at all is the sharper lesson:

```
:91  * 4 of the 30, which is that file's own new `declaredCode` line at the four
:92  * seams.
```

**The phrase is WRAPPED across a line break.** My `git grep "four seams"` this round returned five hits and silently missed this one; my *earlier* grep caught it only because it matched the bare token `four`. ⇒ I had `:91-92` on the list by accident and `:262` off it by construction. ⭐ This is exactly what #12454 exists for — *"the phrase census needs a wrap-tolerant grep"* — and it bit the seat that wrote that card, in the same round.

And the dev's disposition of `:91-92` is right: it is a record of a **past ablation measurement**, and its "four seams" names the *other* file's four **test** seams, which really are four. ⛔ Measured numbers do not get rewritten to fit a later census. Leaving it took more judgement than changing it would have.

### ⚠️ My second error: I repeated the card's reason without checking it, and it is a compression of two different guards

I wrote *"`private async` + `.catch(() => undefined)`"* as if that were one argument. Measured, it is two, and the dev separated them:

- `resolveExecCtx` being **`async`** denies the **synchronous** limb.
- The `.catch()` denies the **rejection** limb.

⭐ And the load-bearing piece is neither: it is the wrapper. I read `packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts:1481` myself —

```ts
resolvePackageRouteExecutionContext(req: any): Promise<any | undefined> {
    const environmentId = req?.params?.environmentId ?? undefined;
    return this.resolveExecCtx(environmentId, req).catch(() => undefined);
}
```

— **not `async`.** So the sync question at that seam was genuinely live and *had* to be measured rather than inherited. Same conclusion, sounder argument. ⛔ A ruling that tells a dev to measure and then hands them a pre-compressed reason is asking them to confirm, not to measure.

Everything else checks out on the tree:
- **`package-routes.ts:81`** — `await options.resolveExecutionContext(req).catch(() => undefined)`. A **second** swallow. ✔
- **`rest-api-plugin.ts:471`** is the only production supplier — I re-grepped `packages/` excluding tests and CHANGELOGs; `direct-mount-composition.ts:126` merely forwards it, and `external-datasource-routes.ts` declares a *different* local option and says so. ✔
- **`registerPackageRoutes` / `PackageRoutesOptions` are not exported** from `packages/rest/src/index.ts` — zero, against a positive control of 17 `export` hits in that same file. ⭐ A zero with a working control. ✔
- ⭐ **The reverse-check I asked for, answered with a tell I had not noticed**: the three production seams inject `async () => { throw error; }` — a *rejection*. The resolver seam injects a **non-`async`** `() => { throw error; }` — a *sync throw*. It has to, because a rejection would be swallowed at `:81` and answer 401. The file was already telling us which seam was different; nobody had read it that way.

### ⚠️ My third error: "155 cases across 4 sections" — measured, it is 58 across 5

`:83` reads *"Measured: 30 failed / 125 passed of 155."* — 30 + 125 = 155. I read an **ablation total from a multi-file run** as this file's case count, and then handed it back as a fact for the dev to verify against. `vitest` says **58**, and the section banners are at `:262`, `:325`, `:392`, `:458`, `:548` — **five**. Both confirmed on `main`.

⇒ three errors this round, all the same shape: **a number I recalled instead of measured, presented with the confidence of one I had.**

### Rulings

**Ruling 4 — `Part of #12537` upheld.** I gave a conditional and the dev checked it rather than picking a side: the swallow is documented at **neither** `rest-server.ts:1483` nor `package-routes.ts:81` — the nearby docblocks explain why the wrapper exists and what an *absent* resolver means, never what a *failing* one means. ⇒ "deliberate" is not established by the code as it stands, so the conditional does not fire and a closing keyword would be wrong. ✔

**Ruling 2 — the case at `:224` is kept and relabelled.** ✔ And the reason is stated **once** in a `Seam census` block and cited from the other five sites rather than copied — which is the shape #12579 spent a whole card establishing.

**The falsifier at `:505` is retired, not reworded** — with a note that if the swallow at `:1483` is ever undone the limb becomes real again and belongs back on the list. ⭐ That is the right disposal: a falsifier that cannot be reached is not a weaker falsifier, it is not one.

**Open question — the test's `name` string: A, agreed.** `'GET /packages — the capability gate resolver throws'` is accurate as it stands, the test-only status is stated directly above it, and ruling 5 said stop rather than widen. ⛔ Do not ride a one-line code change on a diff whose whole verification is a comment-only hash proof. If the marker in raw CI output is wanted, it is a separate one-line PR.

Comment-only proven with the instrument calibrated **both** ways (code-token mutant `080c0989…` DIFFERS; comment-token mutant `8849a4b2…` SAME) — an equality from an uncalibrated instrument is not evidence, and this one is calibrated. Suite green on the real numbers (58 in this file, 105 across both). ⭐ Ratchets **re-run after the final commit** and quoted from *that* run at `HEAD=d496a4301` — a green measured on a tree that is no longer HEAD is not a green. ⭐ And the typecheck coverage is stated precisely rather than implied: the build program reads **0** of this file, the test program reads **1**, so "typecheck is green" is scoped to the program that actually reads it.
